text: Read carefully the poem on the opposite page. The poet depicts a young boy who has climbed a
hill to look out to sea.
How does the poet strikingly convey the boy’s developing thoughts and feelings?
To help you answer this question, you might consider:
• what the boy observes as he looks out to sea
• how the boy imagines what lies beyond
• the contrast between his daydream and his home.
Childhood

OR
Read carefully the following extract from a novel. The speaker, Hortense Joseph, has just arrived
in London. She has travelled from Jamaica by boat to be reunited with her husband Gilbert, who is
not at the dockside to meet her.
In what ways does the writer strikingly convey Hortense’s experiences?
To help you answer this question, you might consider:
• Hortense’s impressions as she waits
• how the writer portrays Hortense’s experience of finding her way to Gilbert’s house
• how she conveys Hortense’s response to Gilbert.
It was two hours I waited for Gilbert.
